div.head: Editions and literature
div.p: A publication, the edition a text was transcribed from or the literature on it, is a biblStruct: in the source description of a file that transcribes an edition (); in the standOff's listBibl, as a record that witnesses and other records point to (); in a manuscript's literature (). The application keeps publications as records modelled on biblatex, related to one another, a text in a volume and a volume in a series, and one kind serves for the editions and the literature. Pages belong to the relation, not to the publication: a council's canons are in Werminghoff's volume at pages 318 to 421, and the volume's record says nothing of them.
The source description's biblStruct is common, since most files transcribe an edition; its entry type and a biblatex key are full.

div.head: A publication's parts
div.p: A biblStruct has up to three parts, each with its title, whose level says which part it belongs to:

list.item: monogr: the publication itself, a book or a volume (its title level m, a second title typed sub where the title page has one) or a journal (j); its authors or editors; its imprint, with the publisher, the place and the date; and, in biblScope, the volume, part or issue, and the pages where the text of the analytic stands;
series: the series the volume belongs to, its title level s, its editor where it has one, and the volume's number in it, in biblScope.

div.p: The edition of the Monumenta Germaniae Historica is the case the parts are made for: a series with its editor, the society that publishes it; a titled volume, edited by a scholar; and in it the texts. The Council of Aachen of 816:

analytic.title: Concilium Aquisgranense a. 816 (mensibus Augusto et Septembri)

editor.orgName: Societas Aperiendis Fontibus Rerum Germanicarum Medii Aevi

div.p: Where the texts of a volume have editors of their own, each analytic names its editor, and the monogr the volume's. The First Council of Constantinople, edited by Adolf Martin Ritter in Giuseppe Alberigo's volume of the Conciliorum Oecumenicorum Generaliumque Decreta:

monogr.title: The oecumenical councils: from Nicaea I to Nicaea II (325-787)

div.p: A title of the wrong level for its part is an error, since the level says what the title is:

div.head: Pages
div.p: A publication has two kinds of pages, and each has its element:

list.item: citedRange, after the monogr and the series, says which pages the file's text comes from: the canons at pages 318 to 421. They're the witness's pages, the relation's. Where the file transcribes the whole text of the analytic, there's none: its pages are the witness's.

div.p: Either may give its range in from and to beside its words. An older edition printed in columns counts columns: the letter of Pope Celestine I to the bishops of Vienne and Narbonne, in Coustant's edition of the popes' letters:

analytic.title: Epistola IV / Caelestini papae I. ad episcopos prouinciae Viennensis & Narbonensis

monogr.title: Epistolae Romanorum pontificum, et quae ad eos scriptae sunt a S. Clemente I. usque ad Innocentium III
Tom. I: ab anno Christi 67 ad annum 440

div.p: The units are a closed list, since each is a field of biblatex: volume, part, issue, page and column. A volume in a series is the volume's number in the series, a tome or a fascicle of it too; an issue is a journal's, a Heft. Another unit fails the RelaxNG:

valItem.desc: a volume; in a series, the volume's number in it

div.p: The application's publications are biblatex's entries, and the import and the exports turn one into the other by the tables below. A publication's entry type is in type, by biblatex's name; where it's missing, the parts say which it is:

table.head: The entry type, where type doesn't give it

div.p: A thesis, a report or a page on the web looks like a book in its parts, and so says what it is by type; an export always does, so that a publication exported and imported again keeps its type. The types are biblatex's, a vocabulary whose seeds are biblatex's own types; another is reported, to be checked or added. div.head: Publications as records
div.p: A publication that more than one thing refers to, the edition several witnesses are in, the catalogue a manuscript's literature cites, is listed once in the standOff's listBibl, with an xml:id, a record's or a placeholder's (new_bibl_ and a name), and pointed to: a witness by a ptr and its pages in citedRange (), a manuscript's literature the same way. The import makes the application's records from a biblStruct: the volume, the text in it and the series, related to one another; then the file's witness, in the publication at the pages of the citedRange. An export writes each publication it points to as a biblStruct with its entry type.

div.head: Reconstructions
div.p: A reconstruction is a text put together from others: a collection known only from what later collections took from it, or a text the project assembles from several editions. Its file's type is reconstruction (), and its source description names the publication it comes from, says in a note that it's a reconstruction, and lists what it was made from in a listWit: the editions, for one the project put together; the manuscripts, for one a scholar made from them. The collection of Benedictus Levita, which the project puts together from Pertz's edition and Schmitz's of the first Additio:

biblStruct.note: A reconstruction: the collection as the project puts it together, from Pertz's edition for the whole text, and from Schmitz's for Additio 1, which Pertz's lacks.

div.p: The import makes the reconstruction a version whose witness is the publication, and joins it to the witnesses it lists. The template reconstruction.xml holds the whole header.
